pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 seat; live chat; unlimited conversations; 0 included AI resolutions.
pricing.billingTerms: Annual public pricing per paid seat; exact month-to-month seat prices were not exposed in the checked page output.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every paid support tier adds $0.49 per AI resolution on top of seat fees; the startup program advertises 86% off and 1 year of Fibi AI free only for qualifying companies founded under 2 years ago with fewer than 6 employees.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Featurebase, run a feedback portal, changelog, roadmap, and lightweight support widget. The hard boundary is integrated suite, ai, custom domains, sso, and hosted delivery, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Collect structured feedback through a portal with a changelog, roadmap, and lightweight support widget, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent status view.
whatYouLose: integrated suite, AI, custom domains, SSO, and hosted delivery
moatNotes: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Featurebase because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Growth plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Featurebase in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect structured feedback through a portal with a changelog, roadmap, and lightweight support widget, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent status view.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
